subject: BYOK readiness & emergency key-rotation playbook — evidence pack
messages:
From: Eleanor Briggs <eleanor.briggs@luminahealth.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: security@luminahealth.com
Date: 2026-11-08T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: BYOK operational controls + emergency rotation evidence

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move into procurement for our platform-wide BYOK requirement, our security team needs a compact evidence package showing how Redwood handles BYOK in production. Can you please provide the following items and any supporting artifacts? Prefered format is a single ZIP of docs/logs plus a short runbook excerpt.

- Emergency key-rotation workflow (steps, roles, max RTO/RPO and expected latency impact)
- Dual-control / split knowledge controls for key import and export (who signs and how)
- HSM export policy and whether remote key export is technically possible (model/version and controls)
- Sample audit log lines for a rotation event (timestamped) and where logs are retained
- TLS cipher suites and mTLS configuration that protect key material in transit between regions
- Cross-region replication behavior for wrapped keys (if applicable) and time-to-replicate
- Zeroization / key destruction confirmation process and evidence retention policy

If you can include an attestation or a short statement for procurement that we can attach to our security review, that would be very helpful.

Target deadline: Nov 15 to stay on track for our security committee next month.

Best,
Eleanor Briggs
Director, Security Operations
LuminaHealth

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Eleanor Briggs <eleanor.briggs@luminahealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-09T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: BYOK operational controls + emergency rotation evidence

Eleanor —

Thanks for the clear list. We can provide a compact bundle and a short attestation for procurement. Ive coordinated with Karthik (infra) and Monica (security ops) and attached three artifacts that address each bullet below: the BYOK ceremony checklist, an HSM export/audit CSV extract, and the rotation runbook excerpt.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Emergency rotation is a documented, automated runbook executed under dual-control (two authorized operators) with an expected RTO of 15-30 minutes for most services; dependent services will experience token refresh/stream interruptions for the duration of the rotation.
- We operate with FIPS-validated HSMs (CloudHSM for hosted and Thales nShield for dedicated/private installs). Remote export of raw key material is blocked by default; any export requires a documented dual-control ceremony, customer approval, and an auditable attestation.
- Audit trails include signed entries for all key lifecycle events (import, wrap/unwrap, rotate, zeroize) retained for 1 year by default and longer under enterprise retention policies.
- TLS: we enforce TLS 1.2/1.3 only; recommended cipher suites (TLS 1.3) and mandatory mTLS between control plane and HSM enclaves. Details are in the attached runbook excerpt.

Attachments included: BYOK-Ceremony-Checklist.pdf (walk-through + roles), HSM-Attestation-Export-Logs.csv (redacted sample logs), rotation-runbook-v1.2.md (excerpt with commands and safety checks).

Next steps: if Lumina wants a signed attestation document on Redwood letterhead, we can produce that (Monica will draft). Also propose a 45-min technical walk-through with Karthik to show a simulated emergency rotation and live log output — any availability next week?

Regards,

So sojin lee
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0121

Soojin —

Appreciate the quick response and the artifacts. A couple of clarifying asks from our security reviewers before we schedule the walk-through:

1) The CSV you attached looks good; can you include a couple of full example log lines (timestamps + event ids) from a rotation exercise rather than redacted columns? We only need sample lines — feel free to mute any PII.
2) For the HSM models: you mentioned CloudHSM and nShield. For our procurement paperwork, can you confirm which model is used in the hosted (SaaS) offering vs private deployments? We need the exact product names/versions so our procurement and compliance teams can verify FIPS/CC certifications.
3) Regarding "remote export": is remote extraction of key material technically impossible in the hosted offering, or is it possible under a controlled ceremony? If possible under ceremony, what controls prevent accidental or unauthorized export (e.g., hardware token presence, offline approvals, KMS policy gates)?
4) Can you share the TTL/lag numbers for cross-region wrapped-key replication (worst-case)?

If you can send those answers and the sample log lines before Friday (2026-11-12) that would help our security committee meet their cutover dates.

Thanks,
Eleanor

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Eleanor Briggs <eleanor.briggs@luminahealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-12T16:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: BYOK operational controls + emergency rotation evidence

Eleanor —

Thanks for the clarifications. See answers inline below and a couple of sample (redacted) log lines taken from a controlled rotation rehearsal we ran in our staging environment this month. If you want live, unredacted output during the walk-through we can run the rehearsal with Lumina observers.

> 1) Can you include a couple of full example log lines (timestamps + event ids) from a rotation exercise rather than redacted columns?

Yes — sample lines (redacted fields with Xs):
2026-11-02T14:08:02Z | EVENT_ID=rot-7b3f | ACTION=KEY_ROTATE_INIT | KEY_ID=xxxxxxxx-xxxx-4xxx-axxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx | USER=operator_01 | METHOD=dual_control_ceremony
2026-11-02T14:12:21Z | EVENT_ID=rot-7b3f | ACTION=KEY_WRAP_UPDATE | KEY_ID=xxxxxxxx-xxxx-4xxx-axxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx | STATUS=SUCCESS | AUDIT_SIG=MEUCIQDx...
2026-11-02T14:15:46Z | EVENT_ID=rot-7b3f | ACTION=KEY_ZEROIZE | KEY_ID=xxxxxxxx-xxxx-4xxx-axxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx | USER=operator_02 | NOTE=post-rotation-zeroize

Logs are signed and stored in our tamper-evident audit store (write-once buckets with object-level encryption) for at least 1 year; retention can be extended on a contract basis. Full log exports include HSM-provided attestation material and signature blocks.

> 2) For the HSM models: which model is used in hosted (SaaS) vs private deployments?

- Hosted (Redwood API / managed tenants): AWS CloudHSM (v3 clusters) — FIPS 140-2 Level 2/3 depending on region and tenancy.
- Dedicated / Private (customer-dedicated appliances / on-prem): Thales nShield Connect (Model XC 4.6 or later) for appliances we ship; customers can also provision customer-owned HSMs (nShield or other FIPS-validated units) when using Private.

We will provide the exact firmware version and recent attestation report for the specific cluster that will be assigned at provisioning time.

> 3) Is remote extraction technically impossible in the hosted offering, or possible under ceremony? What prevents accidental export?

Technical summary: raw key material never leaves the HSM in plaintext. Export of key material as plaintext is blocked by default and cannot be performed by a single operator. Export is possible only under an explicit dual-control ceremony, which requires:
- Two distinct hardware tokens (YubiKey-style OTP) present and used by two authorized operators;
- An offline approval record (signed approval PDF stored in our compliance vault) attached to the ceremony;
- Automated KMS policy gates that require a multi-signature transaction to transition the key state to "exportable" for a limited window;
- HSM-level operator authentication and an operator-limited window (typically 5 minutes) after which the window closes;
- All export attempts are recorded with HSM attestation blobs and forwarded to the customer audit endpoint if configured.

For hosted customers we recommend against any plaintext export; we will only enable export under customer-authorized, contractually-approved ceremonies with additional escrow controls.

> 4) TTL/lag numbers for cross-region wrapped-key replication (worst-case)?

Typical replication observed: 1-3 seconds for metadata, 10-45 seconds for wrapped-key propagation under normal load. Worst-case (high load / transient network issues): up to 10 minutes. We document replication windows in the runbook and add a grace period to rotation operations to avoid split-brain.

Action items:
- Monica will prepare a short signed attestation PDF on Redwood letterhead outlining the export controls and retention policy (deliverable: Nov 15).
- Karthik will schedule the technical walk-through and can run an unredacted rehearsal if Lumina signs a non-disclosure addendum (NDA) / observer agreement.
- Ive uploaded the supporting artifacts to the shared drive: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/LUM-2026/BYOK-evidence

If that covers your asks well follow up with the signed attestation and proposed meeting times.

Cheers,

So sojin lee
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
